newsitem.title: YEMEN: Progress made in efforts to free Germans in Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Progress made in efforts to free Germans in Yemen.

text.p: Negotiations with the kidnappers of seven Germans in Yemen are making progress and the tribesmen are seeking government amnesty before freeing the hostages, a top security official said on Monday.

"Negotiations with the kidnappers are making progress without the government making any concessions," the official told Reuters. He said security forces have tightened the siege on the area where the hostages are being held.

He said the tribesmen, who have been holding the seven German men aged between 30 and 45 since last Monday, were now seeking "a government amnesty and guarantees they would not be arrested after releasing the hostages."
The German men were kidnapped while riding motorcycles through the Wadi al-Dabaat area between Mahra and Hadramaut provinces, 770 km (480 miles) east of of the capital Sanaa.

Official sources had said the kidnappers, all local tribesmen, wanted to put pressure on the government to bring to justice an alleged Yemeni swindler who sold them smuggled cars brought in from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states.
They said the abductors were demanding a 12 million marks ($7 million) ransom, but Hadramaut police denied that.
Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners in recent years to use as bargaining chips.
An American diplomat and a Saudi ambassador have been among the kidnap victims. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions and all the hostages have been released unharmed.
Some were rescued by security forces, others were set free.
